name: True Colour (Natural RGB)
recommendedUse: Visual context, smoke plume tracking, and landform orientation.
caveats: Cannot penetrate dense smoke haze or cloud cover. Fails to separate shadow from low-severity burn.

name: False Colour SWIR (Burn Scar Emphasis)
recommendedUse: Penetrating atmospheric smoke and clearly delineating actively burning fronts and charred ground.
caveats: 20m spatial resolution. Exposed dry soil or bare rock can display reflectance similar to fire scars.

name: NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index)
recommendedUse: Measuring canopy photosynthetic vigor and post-fire ecological recovery trajectory.
caveats: Severe drought and seasonal curing reduce NDVI significantly, even in completely unburnt canopies.

name: dNBR (Differenced Normalized Burn Ratio)
formula: NBR = (B8A - B12) / (B8A + B12); dNBR = NBR_pre - NBR_post
recommendedUse: Standard satellite metric for fire severity classification (unburnt, low, moderate, high).
caveats: Requires pre-fire and post-fire cloud-free imagery. Agricultural mowing or logging mimics fire damage.
